component.name: PackWarden
component.summary: Uninstall packages in bulk on any distribution

description.p: PackWarden lists every application installed on your system, from pacman, APT, DNF and Flatpak, in a single window, and lets you select and remove them in bulk. It works the same on every distribution. Experienced users get one fast tool instead of separate package manager and cleanup commands. If you are coming from Windows, it is the Bulk Crap Uninstaller you have been missing.

ul.li: One list for all package managers: pacman, APT, DNF, Flatpak
Also manages game libraries: Steam, Heroic (Epic, GOG) and Lutris
Search, filter by source, sort by installed size
Batch uninstall with a single confirmation
Secure privilege handling through polkit (pkexec)

description.p: An improvement and bug-fix release, focused on making updates and app removal more reliable and more honest about what actually happened.

ul.li: Snap apps' own saved data, stored outside the usual cache and settings folders, is now found and included when choosing to back up before removal.
The Cancel button can no longer be clicked while a removal is in progress, so it never gives the false impression that it stopped something.

If removing packages through one package manager is cancelled or denied, apps that were successfully removed through a different package manager in the same batch are now reported correctly, instead of the whole operation being marked as cancelled.
If every app is removed successfully but cleaning up a single leftover file fails, PackWarden now says that clearly, instead of implying the apps themselves failed to be removed.
Removing a Flatpak app that's installed both system-wide and per-user no longer triggers an incorrect "an installed app was affected" warning.
A Wine program's registry entry is now clearly marked in the interface as always removed together with the program and never included in a backup.
"Check for Updates" is no longer shown when PackWarden wasn't installed through its own installer, since it wouldn't be able to update that copy anyway.
Package names that include an architecture or slot suffix weren't correctly matched against the critical-system-package protection list.
PackWarden's own installation folder was sometimes listed as a leftover of itself.
Some Nix package version numbers with more than one hyphen were parsed incorrectly.
The built-in updater now keeps your previous installation safely aside while installing an update, and automatically restores it if the update fails or is interrupted partway through.
Redesigned the main window's top bar with a traditional title bar and a classic File / Tools / Help menu bar.
Added the ability to ignore individual programs from the Unused Programs list, with a dedicated panel to review and restore them later.
Added column visibility toggle and a name filter panel, both from a right-click on a column header.
Added a "Location" column showing the real path to a program's main executable.
Added support for Windows programs installed through Wine as a new package source, with real icons, desktop shortcuts, and dedicated leftover categories.
Added automatic license detection from GitHub for Flatpak apps that don't publish one through their store listing.
Lutris games now show their real icon and which store they came from, matching Steam and Heroic games.
Launching an app now reports a real reason when it fails, instead of failing silently.
The in-app language setting now also applies to GTK/Adwaita's own built-in interface text.
Background usage detection (Settings → Privacy) didn't actually work when PackWarden was installed via install.sh; the background service was never set up.
Removing a Steam game could leave it still showing as installed in Steam until Steam was restarted.
GOG and Amazon games listed through Heroic were read from the wrong file.
Removing an Epic game through Heroic never actually worked, due to a wrong config path.
Heroic games weren't detected at all on some installations, such as Arch Linux's heroic-games-launcher package.
Added optional background usage detection (Settings → Privacy) so the Unused Programs list stays accurate even while PackWarden is closed. Off by default, fully local, no network access.

Removing a Flatpak app now also cleans up the shared data Flatpak leaves behind after an app is uninstalled (shown as "Trash Data" in some other app stores). Automatic, part of the normal removal process.
Games installed through Steam, Heroic, or Lutris weren't covered by usage tracking at all. An actively played game could still be wrongly listed under Unused Programs.
Some Steam games installed to a second drive or library showed a generic icon instead of their real one.
Renamed "Unused Apps" to "Unused Programs", since the list already includes games alongside regular applications.
Time labels like "1 days ago" now correctly read "1 day ago".
A few interface texts stayed in English regardless of the selected language.
Added support for Steam, Heroic (Epic, GOG) and Lutris game libraries — list and remove games alongside your regular packages, in the same window.
Steam games now show their real version number (build ID) instead of a blank field.
Games installed in a secondary Steam library (a different drive or folder than the default) were not showing up in the list.
Removing a Steam or Heroic game left its desktop and menu shortcut behind, still showing the game's icon after it was gone.
Removing a Steam game left its Workshop content and shader cache on disk.
Leftover-file detection could miss a package's settings folder when its name was written slightly differently on disk (e.g. spaces removed).
The "Unused apps" time threshold (3 months, 6 months, 1 year, or a custom period) reset every time the window was opened instead of remembering your last choice.
Leftover file cleanup now moves files to the Trash instead of deleting them permanently, so an accidental selection can be undone.
Protection against removing critical packages now also considers how many other installed packages depend on it, not just a fixed list of known-critical names.
The built-in updater now verifies a checksum before installing an update, and only installs a deliberately published release instead of the latest development commit.

description.p: First release: pacman, APT, DNF and Flatpak support with bulk removal.
